intro: When you search for a smile makeover near me, you're likely thinking about changing how your smile looks and want to find a private dentist who can guide you through the options. A smile makeover combines treatments such as aligners, whitening, bonding and veneers to achieve an agreed result, so the first step is a proper conversation about what you hope to achieve. We can introduce you to a suitable UK professional who will quote you directly, with prices on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a smile makeover near me usually need
need_lead: Most people want a local private dentist who can assess their smile, explain the possible treatments and give a clear plan and quote.
needs: You may feel self-conscious about chipped, stained or uneven teeth and want a dentist who can discuss several options rather than just one treatment.
You might have looked at pictures of smile makeovers online and want to know which of those results are realistic for your own teeth and gums.
You could be unsure whether you need orthodontics, whitening, bonding or veneers, and want a dentist to explain the sequence and why one might come before another.
You may have a special occasion coming up and want to understand what can be done in the time available, without being rushed into decisions.
You might have had treatment before that didn't meet your expectations and want a careful assessment before committing to anything further.
context_heading: What to understand about smile makeovers
context: A smile makeover is not a single treatment but a plan that combines procedures such as aligners, whitening, bonding and veneers to reach an agreed result. Planning comes first, and the sequence matters because some treatments work best when done before others. A good dentist will discuss realistic expectations with you rather than promising a perfect outcome.

Dentists, dental hygienists, dental therapists and dental nurses must be registered with the General Dental Council (GDC), and you can check the GDC register online. Private clinics providing regulated healthcare in England must register with the Care Quality Commission (CQC), which inspects and publishes ratings; in Wales the regulator is Healthcare Inspectorate Wales, in Scotland Healthcare Improvement Scotland, and in Northern Ireland the RQIA. If something goes wrong with private dental treatment, start with the practice's complaints process, and the Dental Complaints Service can help with complaints that are not resolved.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe what you would like to change about your smile, such as colour, shape, gaps or crowding, so we can introduce you to a dentist who suits your needs.
Mention any previous dental treatment you have had, including orthodontics or cosmetic work, as this can affect the planning.
Say whether you have any particular deadline or event in mind, so the dentist can discuss what is realistic.
Let us know if you have any dental anxiety or need extra time, so we can introduce you to a practice that can accommodate this.
Tell us your general location and how far you are willing to travel for appointments.
Include any current dental concerns, such as sensitivity or gum problems, as these may need to be addressed before a makeover.
questions: What treatments would you recommend for my smile, and in what order would they be carried out?
What are the realistic outcomes and limitations of each option for my teeth?
How will you assess my dental health before starting any cosmetic treatment?
What are the costs involved, and will I receive a written treatment plan and quote?
What aftercare and follow-up will be needed, and how long should the results last?
What are the risks and possible complications of the treatments you are suggesting?

faqs.a: A smile makeover is a combination of treatments such as aligners, whitening, bonding and veneers planned together to improve the appearance of your smile. It is tailored to your individual needs and agreed with your dentist.

faqs.q: How do I choose a dentist for a smile makeover?
faqs.a: Check that the dentist is registered with the General Dental Council (GDC) and, in England, that the practice is registered with the Care Quality Commission (CQC). Ask about their experience with the treatments you are considering and whether they can show you examples of their work.

faqs.q: Is a smile makeover available on the NHS?
faqs.a: Smile makeovers are generally considered cosmetic and are usually provided privately. Some treatments may be available on the NHS if there is a clinical need, but this depends on your individual circumstances and local NHS rules.

faqs.q: What should I do if I am unhappy with private dental treatment?
faqs.a: Start with the practice's complaints process. If the issue is not resolved, the Dental Complaints Service can help with private dental complaints.
